form_name: United States Estate (and Generation-Skipping Transfer) Tax Return
rule: Due 9 months after the date of death; not a fixed calendar date
description: Form 706 is due 9 months after the decedent's date of death, so there is no single fixed 2026 calendar date - it depends on when the death occurred. Form 4768 grants an automatic 6-month extension of time to file. A late portability election may be available within 5 years of death under Rev. Proc. 2022-32.
authority: IRS Instructions for Form 706 (2026 update fetched this session): "You must file Form 706 to report estate and/or GST tax within 9 months after the date of the decedent's death." Extension: Form 4768 grants an automatic 6-month extension.

form_name: United States Gift (and Generation-Skipping Transfer) Tax Return
filer: Individuals who made reportable gifts during the tax year
rule: Same due date as the individual income tax return
extension_form: Automatic with a 1040 extension, or Form 8892 if not extending the income tax return
description: Form 709 for 2025 gifts is due April 15, 2026. An extension of the donor's 2025 Form 1040 automatically extends the Form 709 due date; if the income tax return is not being extended, Form 8892 requests a separate automatic 6-month extension. Extensions to file do not extend the deadline to pay any gift or GST tax due.
authority: IRS Instructions for Form 709: "Generally, you must file Form 709 no earlier than January 1, but not later than April 15, of the year after the gift was made."

form_name: Return of Organization Exempt From Income Tax / Short Form / Private Foundation
rule: 15th day of the 5th month after the close of the accounting period
description: For a calendar-year exempt organization, Form 990, 990-EZ, or 990-PF for tax year 2025 is due May 15, 2026. Form 8868 provides an automatic 6-month extension to November 15, 2026.
authority: IRS: "Form 990, 990-EZ, or 990-PF must be filed by the 15th day of the 5th month after the end of your organization's accounting period." Form 8868 grants an automatic 6-month extension.

form_name: Electronic Notice (e-Postcard) for Tax-Exempt Organizations Not Required to File Form 990 or 990-EZ
filer: Small tax-exempt organizations (calendar year, gross receipts normally $50,000 or less)
rule: 15th day of the 5th month after the close of the accounting period
description: Form 990-N for a calendar-year small exempt organization is due May 15, 2026, same as the 990/990-EZ/990-PF due date. Unlike those forms, the 990-N due date cannot be extended - there is no extension mechanism, though the IRS states there is no penalty for late submission unless it is the organization's third consecutive missed year (which triggers automatic revocation of exempt status).
authority: IRS: "The 990-N due date cannot be extended, but there is no penalty for submitting it late unless it's the third (and only) year."

form_name: Statement of Specified Foreign Financial Assets
filer: Individuals (and certain entities) with specified foreign financial assets above the reporting threshold
rule: Files attached to the taxpayer's income tax return; no independent due date
description: Form 8938 has no due date of its own - it is attached to and filed by the due date (including extensions) of the taxpayer's income tax return (Form 1040, 1120, 1065, etc.). It does not appear as its own calendar entry because its date always matches whichever income tax return it is attached to.
authority: IRS Instructions for Form 8938: "Attach Form 8938 to your annual return and file by the due date (including extensions) for that return."

form_name: Return of U.S. Persons With Respect to Certain Foreign Partnerships
filer: U.S. persons with certain interests in foreign partnerships
rule: Files attached to the filer's income tax return (or partnership/exempt-org return); no independent due date
description: Form 8865 has no due date of its own - it is attached to and filed by the due date (including extensions) of the filer's income tax return (or partnership/exempt organization return, as applicable). If the filer is not otherwise required to file an income tax return, Form 8865 must be filed separately by the date a return would have been due.
authority: IRS Instructions for Form 8865: "Attach Form 8865 to your income tax return (or, if applicable, partnership or exempt organization return) and file both by the due date (including extensions) for that return."

form_name: Heavy Highway Vehicle Use Tax Return
filer: Owners of heavy highway vehicles (55,000 lbs+ gross weight) first used in the given month
rule: Due by the last day of the month following first use in July 2026
description: Form 2290 for a vehicle first used on a public highway during July 2026 is due 2026-08-31, per the IRS Instructions for Form 2290's month-of-first-use filing table for the July 2026 - June 2027 tax period. If a due date falls on a weekend or legal holiday, the return is due the next business day.
authority: IRS Instructions for Form 2290 (July 2026 - June 2027 tax period filing table): "file by the last day of the month following the month of first use."
